title: Signal Harmonizer and Pin Priority Router for model-catalog intake
creator: Evan Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers send heterogeneous onboarding requests (new models, pin/version requests, deprecations, quantized variants). Triage is manual, slow, and inconsistent: PM/Eng/Support spend significant time clarifying security/compliance constraints and routing to the correct eval lane. Outcome: delays, missed SLAs, and occasional incorrect pinning decisions that cause downstream instability.

Goal: Build a deterministic intake layer that harmonizes customer signals and applies a configurable Pin Priority Router to automatically suggest (and in defined cases auto-apply) onboarding lanes: fast-path, canary, pinned-stable, deprecation-quarantine. The system should reduce manual triage time, improve routing accuracy, and capture reasons for overrides for auditability.
proposal:
1) Signal Harmonizer: consolidate and canonicalize incoming signals for each submission: security requirements (regulatory, data residency), SLA target, estimated qps/throughput, revenue tier, partner vs internal, model family/quantization flag, test-suite pass rate, and historical usage if replacing an existing pinned model. Use deterministic scoring rules and a small ML classifier for ambiguous cases.

2) Pin Priority Router: map harmonized signals to recommended onboarding lanes and an assigned priority (P0-P3). Rules are configurable via a simple policy table and support overrides. Actions include suggested eval gate (full eval, lite-eval, canary), auto-pin eligibility, deprecation delay window, and whether encrypted/offline deployment is required.

3) Operational UX: a triage UI in the Console that shows harmonized signals, explains routing rationale, and enables one-click overrides and audit logging. Provide a shadow mode that logs recommendations without changing current process.

4) Telemetry and feedback loop: capture when recommendations are overridden and why; feed back into policy iterations and classifier retraining.

Implementation pieces: intake schema updates, lightweight classifier service (rule-first), policy engine for mapping signals to lanes, Console triage UI, metrics/dashboard, and an API for programmatic requests from enterprise onboarding flows.
success_metrics: Reduce average manual triage time per request from 45m to 25m within first quarter after rollout
Automatically classify and route >= 85% of enterprise model requests correctly (based on later human-confirmed labels) within 2 months of launch
Decrease incorrect pin application incidents by 50% in the quarter after rollout
Shadow-mode coverage for at least 30 days with at least 300 enterprise requests logged before full enforcement
acceptance_criteria: Signal Harmonizer accepts canonical intake payload and returns normalized signal vector for 95% of sample submissions
Pin Priority Router returns lane recommendation and priority for synthetic test suite covering edge cases (security, high qps, partial eval pass) with expected outputs
Console triage view shows harmonized signals and recommended action, and supports manual override which is persisted to audit logs
Shadow mode runs for minimum 30 days and captures override reasons in at least 60% of override events
Documentation and runbook published: triage decision guidelines, policy table, and rollback process
scope: In-scope: intake schema, rule-policy engine, lightweight classifier proof-of-concept, triage Console UI, telemetry dashboard, shadow mode. Out-of-scope: full ML-powered automated pinning across all customers (future work), deep model eval infra changes, billing changes for pinned variants.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-automation could mis-route safety-sensitive requests. Mitigation: conservative default policies and mandatory manual review for high-risk signals (security/compliance=true).
Risk: Classifier drift. Mitigation: start with rule-first design and keep classifier in advisory role with human-in-the-loop retraining cadence every 6 weeks.
Risk: Insufficient instrumentation for override reasons. Mitigation: require a short structured reason field on override and track it in telemetry prior to enforcement.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design and policy table (2 weeks). Phase 1: Implement Signal Harmonizer + policy engine + Console triage view in shadow mode (4 weeks). Phase 2: Run shadow mode for 30 days, gather telemetry, iterate policies (4 weeks). Phase 3: Soft enforcement for non-safety lanes + monitoring (2 weeks). Phase 4: Full enforcement for applicable low-risk autopinning lanes with manual approval for high-risk (2 weeks).
test_plan: Unit tests for schema normalization, policy table unit tests, end-to-end integration tests exercising sample enterprise requests, manual QA sessions with Solutions and Support teams, and a pilot with 3 enterprise customers in shadow mode.
notes: Pilot candidates: AcmeCorp, HealthSync, FinAPI — suggested by AE team
